docs.text: Welcome to Scientific Computing at RU! This website hosts documentation on HPC access and scientific computing resources avialable to the faculty and students of Reykjavik University. It is built by the people who use these resources. Join our chatroom (see below) and consider contributing content. Check the news for upcoming events. Available compute resources A non-exhaustive list of resources available to RU is below. Local HPC cluster Documentation and access instructions. IREI resources Reykjavik University is a parner to the Icelandic Research e-Infratructure (IRE) project , and has access to its resources, including HPC clusters and the IREI cloud. See www.irei.is for more information. HPC documentation for the Elja cluster. Acquiring access to Elja. Large-scale computing resources Reykjavik University has access to large-scale computing resources at the LUMI supercomputer in Finland and other sites funded by the European High-Performance Computing Joint Undertaking ( EuroHPC JU ). Join our chatroom! A Discord server was created as a support channel for everyone who deals with HPC or scientific computing at RU, including both students and faculty. The following invite link works without restructions and will be valid until 2026-06-03: https://discord.gg/qYtuZRdP . Please join now! After this time, a new method for joining the server will be provided.

docs.text: Contributing to this site The content on this website is created by people at RU who do hands-on scientific computing or work with HPC clusters. If you solved a problem you encountered, or are able to write documentation or tutorials broadly useful to your peers at RU, please consider contributing to this website. All content is hosted on GitHub, where you will find specific contrubution instructions .

docs.text: Time: May 27, Wednesday, 13:00 Location: M101 At this event, Elvar Örn Jónsson from HÍ will tell us about the Icelandic Research e-Infratructure (IREI) project that RU is a partner to. Everyone is welcome! The event will be of particular interest to those who have intensive computing or data storage needs, beyond what our local infrastructure at RU can easily support. We are also launching a Scientific Computing User Group at Reykjavik University. The goal is to connect people who make use of HPC or scientific computing, share expertise and experiences, and support each others’ work. Join us on Wednesday if you are interested. Abstract: The Icelandic Research E-Infrastucture (IREI) project, hosted at the Division of Information Technology University of Iceland, provides general IT resources to publicly funded research in Iceland. IREI provides access to powerful high-performance computing (HPC) clusters, secure data storage and sharing-platform solutions, and installation and implementation of scientific software and virtual environments. IREI partners include UI, RU, Veðurstofan, Landspítali, as well as several others. This talk will introduce available IREI resources, and means to access them, to the faculty and staff of RU.
docs.title: Introduction to IREI, HPC and scientific computing resources
